sn1.71:1.2: As she was standing to one side, a devatā recited this verse to the Blessed One:
sn1.71:2.1:
“Having killed what
do you sleep in ease?
sn1.71:2.2:
Having killed what
do you not grieve?
sn1.71:2.3:
Of the slaying
of what one thing
sn1.71:3.1:
The Buddha:
“Having killed anger
you sleep in ease.
sn1.71:3.2:
Having killed anger
you do not grieve.
sn1.71:3.5:
The noble ones praise
the slaying of anger
—with its honeyed crest
& poison root—
sn1.71:3.6:
for having killed it
you do not grieve.”
